questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following:

(i) Central bank

(ii) Cheque

(iii) Collateral

(iv) Token coin

2+2+2+2 = (8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** These terms are basic in money and banking.

**(i) Central bank (2 marks).** The **apex (main) bank of a country**, or of a group of countries, which controls the banking system and the money supply, issues the currency, acts as banker to the government and to the commercial banks, and carries out monetary policy. Example: the BEAC for the CEMAC countries, or the Bank of England.

**(ii) Cheque (2 marks).** A **written order from a customer (the drawer) to his bank to pay a stated sum of money** to a named person (the payee) or to the bearer, out of the money in his current account.

**(iii) Collateral (2 marks).** An **asset (for example a house, land or a vehicle) that a borrower pledges to the lender as security for a loan**. If the borrower fails to repay, the lender may take and sell the asset to recover the money.

**(iv) Token coin (2 marks).** A **coin whose face (nominal) value is greater than the value of the metal it contains**, so that it is accepted because of the law and the confidence of the public and not because of its metal. Most coins in use today are token coins.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State and explain Three (03) advantages of using a cheque.

(ii) Explain Three (03) functions of BEAC to member countries.

(6 marks for (i), 6 marks for (ii))
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three advantages of using a cheque (6 marks)**

1. **Safety.** Carrying a cheque is safer than carrying a large sum of cash, which can be lost or stolen. A cheque can be **crossed** so that it is paid only into a bank account, and the money cannot be taken by a thief.

2. **Convenience for large and long-distance payments.** A cheque can be written for any amount and sent by post, so large payments can be made without counting or carrying notes, and a debt can be settled in another town.

3. **A record and proof of payment.** The cheque counterfoil and the bank statement show to whom, when and how much was paid, and the paid cheque is a receipt. This helps in keeping accounts and settling disputes.

(Other correct points: the exact amount can be written, so no change is needed; and it can be stopped if lost.)

**(ii) Three functions of BEAC to its member countries (6 marks)**

BEAC (the Bank of Central African States) is the **central bank** of the CEMAC member countries, which share a common currency.

1. **Issuing the common currency.** BEAC has the sole right to issue the currency used by the member countries (the CFA franc of Central Africa), so that all the members share the same money.

2. **Carrying out the common monetary policy.** It controls the money supply, credit and interest rates in the whole zone, in order to maintain the stability of the value of the currency and to control inflation.

3. **Banker to the governments and to the commercial banks.** It keeps the accounts of the member governments and of the commercial banks, gives them loans and advances within set limits, and acts as the lender of last resort to banks in difficulty.

(Other correct functions: keeping and managing the common reserves of foreign exchange, and organising the payment and clearing system between the member countries.)

**Conclusion.** Cheques make payments safe and convenient, while BEAC provides a common currency and a common monetary policy for the member countries.
